'''Caroline Colijn''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|FRSC}} is a Canadian mathematician and epidemiologist. She is a Tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] in Mathematics for Infection, Evolution and Public Health at [[Simon Fraser University]] (SFU).

==Early life and education==
Colijn earned her [[undergraduate degree]] from the [[University of British Columbia]] before enrolling at [[York University]] for her [[Master's degree]] in environmental studies and the [[University of Waterloo]] for her PhD.<ref>{{cite web |title=SFU celebrates arrival of first Canada 150 Research Chair |url=http://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2018/08/sfu-celebrates-arrival-of-first-canada-150-research-chair-.html |website=sfu.ca |publisher=Simon Fraser University |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=August 16, 2018}}</ref> She completed her post-doctoral training with [[Michael Mackey]] at [[McGill University]] and later studied epidemiology with [[Megan B. Murray|Megan Murray]] at the [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]].<ref name = "magpie">{{cite web |title=The MAGPIE Group |url=https://www.sfu.ca/magpie/people.html |website=sfu.ca |publisher=Simon Fraser University |accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
Following her post-doctoral training, Colijn joined the [[University of Bristol]]'s Department of Engineering Maths until 2011 when she moved to [[Imperial College London]].<ref name = "magpie"/> While at Imperial College London, Colijn earned an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Fellowship in order to study how to improve scientists ability to infer the ecological processes shaping a pathogen's evolution.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr Caroline Colijn |url=https://epsrc.ukri.org/about/people/carolinecolijn/ |website=epsrc.ukri.org |publisher=[[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] |accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref>

In 2017, the [[Government of Canada]] announced the hiring of four Canada 150 Research Chairs, including Colijn.<ref>{{cite web |title=B.C. gains 2 world-renowned scientists as part of new federal hiring initiative |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/b-c-gains-2-world-renowned-scientists-as-part-of-new-federal-hiring-initiative-1.4446789 |website=cbc.ca |publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=December 13, 2017}}</ref> The program's initiative was to "enhance Canada's reputation as a global centre for science, research and innovation excellence" and Colijn's focus at [[Simon Fraser University]] (SFU) was on making "connections between mathematics and public health, using diverse data to understand how pathogens adapt and spread."<ref>{{cite web |title=International public health mathematician to join SFU as Canada 150 Research Chair |url=https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2017/12/international-public-health-mathematician-to-join-sfu-as-canada-.html |website=sfu.ca |publisher=Simon Fraser University |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=December 13, 2017}}</ref> 

[[File:Caroline Colijn 2020.jpg|thumb|left|Colijn in 2020]]
In February 2020, Colijn, [[Jukka Corander]], and [[Nick Croucher]] published a study in the journal ''[[Nature Microbiology]]'' regarding vaccines. They proposed a new method for choosing the best vaccine to fight and eliminate certain bacterial strains using genomic data and mathematical modelling.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sharma |first1=Shradhha |title=Pioneering SFU research customizes vaccines to reduce bacterial disease |url=https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2020/02/pioneering-sfu-research-customizes-vaccines-to-reduce-bacterial-.html |website=sfu.ca |publisher=Simon Fraser University|accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=February 3, 2020}}</ref> 

During the [[COVID-19 pandemic in British Columbia]],  Colijn was awarded a Genome British Columbia grant to map the spread of [[COVID-19]] in British Columbia. Leading a group of researchers, Colijn used the grant to measure how successful and effective British Columbia's health policy measures in lowering the risk of COVID-19.<ref>{{cite web |title=SFU epidemiologist awarded Genome B.C. grant to develop COVID-19 statistical tool |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-05/sfu-ser050520.php |website=eurekalert.org |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=May 5, 2020 |archive-date=June 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200618194639/https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-05/sfu-ser050520.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> 
Colijn spoke favorably of the effectiveness of random testing and used mathematical modelling to project high-risk trends in the province, allowing health officers to better determine how to effectively treat the pandemic.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bhathal |first1=Harvin |title=BC's COVID-19 health policies are being informed by SFU professor's research |url=https://the-peak.ca/2020/05/bcs-covid-19-health-policies-are-being-informed-by-sfu-professors-research/ |website=the-peak.ca |publisher=The Peak |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=May 18, 2020}}</ref> Colijn explained that "the role of mathematical modelling in infectious disease epidemiology is to think about the data we have at the population level, groups of people, links between the groups, rates of infection and case counts, and thinking about what that means for the dynamics of this thing going forward."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Burgees |first1=Steve |title=She Plots the Possible Arcs of the Pandemic |url=https://thetyee.ca/News/2020/03/26/Pandemic-Plot-Arc/ |website=thetyee.ca |publisher=[[The Tyee]] |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref> She was also selected by the [[Chief Science Advisor (Canada)|Chief Science Advisor of Canada]] [[Mona Nemer]] to sit on a country wide science expert panel to advise on COVID-19-related scientific developments.<ref>{{cite web |title=COVID-19 Expert Panel |url=http://www.science.gc.ca/eic/site/063.nsf/eng/h_98013.html |website=science.gc.ca |accessdate=June 17, 2020}}</ref> In this role, she published a research paper titled ''Estimating the impact of COVID-19 control measures using a Bayesian model of physical distancing,'' which concluded that keeping a physical distance had a direct impact on overall contact rates in the population.<ref>{{cite web |title=SFU epidemiologist's research informs B.C. health policy on COVID-19 |url=https://www.sfu.ca/sfunews/stories/2020/05/sfu-epidemiologist-s-research-informs-b-c--health-policy-on-covi.html |website=sfu.ca |publisher=Simon Fraser University |accessdate=June 17, 2020 |date=May 5, 2020}}</ref> In 2025, Colijn was appointed a Tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] in Mathematics for Infection, Evolution and Public Health.<ref>{{cite web |title=Caroline Colijn |url=https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=6020 |publisher=Government of Canada |access-date=September 26, 2025}}</ref>
